requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full bases placed in a straight line: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:2,0,0;full – contiguous q=0,1,2 r=0 L0, forming a 3-cell row. Verified by get_build counts piece:3.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Bin in each cell using drained variant: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain – hex-bin-full-drain has drainage holes in floor.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for herbs (planted/dressed as herb planter)
requirements.evidence: All three bins filled with soil and planted: bin:0,0,0 with basil-young (prop:1), bin:1,0,0 with mint-young (prop:2), bin:2,0,0 with parsley-young (prop:3). Visible in look az45 polar62 and polar10.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell linear planter (0,0,0 +1,0,0 +2,0,0) with a full-depth drained bin in each cell. Bins are hex-bin-full-drain with drain holes. Each bin filled with soil and planted with a young herb plug (basil, mint, parsley) to show herb use. Caps closed all 14 open outer faces and joint bolts lock the two joints; check_build clear, meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three side-by-side herb bays, each draining — I'll design your planter.
